{{Short description|Endofunctor on the category V of finite-dimensional vector spaces}}
In algebra, a '''polynomial functor''' is an [[endofunctor]] on the [[category of vector spaces|category <math>\mathcal{V}</math> of finite-dimensional vector spaces]] that depends polynomially on vector spaces. For example, the [[symmetric power]]s <math>V \mapsto \operatorname{Sym}^n(V)</math> and the [[exterior power]]s <math>V \mapsto \wedge^n(V)</math> are polynomial functors from <math>\mathcal{V}</math> to <math>\mathcal{V}</math>; these two are also [[Schur functor]]s.

The notion appears in [[representation theory]] as well as [[category theory]] (the [[calculus of functors]]). In particular, the category of homogeneous polynomial functors of degree ''n'' is equivalent to the [[category of representations|category of finite-dimensional representations]] of the [[symmetric group]] <math>S_n</math> over a field of characteristic zero.<ref>{{harvnb|Macdonald|1995|loc=Ch. I, Appendix A: 5.4.}}</ref>

== Definition ==
Let ''k'' be a [[Field (mathematics)|field]] of [[Characteristic (algebra)|characteristic]] zero and <math>\mathcal{V}</math> the [[Category (mathematics)|category]] of finite-dimensional ''k''-[[Vector space|vector spaces]] and ''k''-[[Linear map|linear maps]]. Then an [[endofunctor]] <math>F\colon \mathcal{V} \to \mathcal{V}</math> is a ''polynomial functor'' if the following equivalent conditions hold:
*For every pair of vector spaces ''X'', ''Y'' in <math>\mathcal{V}</math>, the map <math>F\colon \operatorname{Hom}(X, Y) \to \operatorname{Hom}(F(X), F(Y))</math> is a [[polynomial mapping]] (i.e., a vector-valued polynomial in linear forms).
*Given linear maps <math>f_i: X \to Y, \, 1 \le i \le r</math> in <math>\mathcal{V}</math>, the function <math>(\lambda_1, \dots, \lambda_r) \mapsto F(\lambda_1 f_1 + \cdots + \lambda_r f_r)</math> defined on <math>k^r</math> is a polynomial function with [[Coefficient|coefficients]] in <math>\operatorname{Hom}(F(X), F(Y))</math>.

A polynomial functor is said to be ''[[homogeneous function|homogeneous]] of degree ''n if for any linear maps <math>f_1, \dots, f_r</math> in <math>\mathcal{V}</math> with common domain and codomain, the vector-valued polynomial <math>F(\lambda_1 f_1 + \cdots + \lambda_r f_r)</math> is homogeneous of degree ''n''.

== Variants ==
If “finite vector spaces” is replaced by “finite sets”, one gets the notion of [[combinatorial species]] (to be precise, those of polynomial nature).
